title: Steer-to-Detect: Probing Hidden Representations for Detection of LLM-Generated Texts
claim: A two-phase procedure first steers a frozen model's representations to separate classes, then thresholds a score for detection.
layout: Two stacked rows (train/test), left-to-right flow, with a layer-detail inset at left
description: The figure is a two-row pipeline split by a dashed horizontal line into Phase I (top, training) and Phase II (bottom, testing). On the left, a light-blue inset zooms into one transformer layer. It shows a stack of blocks: multi-head self-attention, add and layernorm, feed-forward MLP, and add and layernorm. A STEERING VECTOR box feeds dashed arrows into the layers. In the main flow, a rounded Train Data box (red LLM-generated and green human-written text) points to three tall frozen observer-LLM columns. A shaded band marks the steered layer, and a STEERING box sends a gradient-update arrow back. Next come 2-D scatter plots of green and red clusters, with a diagonal separating line and mean-direction diamonds. The last step is a scoring function, shown as overlapping green and red density curves in Phase I. In Phase II, the curves are well separated by a dashed calibrated-threshold line. A legend sits along the bottom.
caption: Overview of Steer-to-Detect (S2D). Phase I (top row) applies a steering vector to reshape the observer LLM’s hidden representations, enhancing the separation between human-written and LLM-generated text. Phase II (bottom row) scores unseen texts and rejects the null hypothesis when the score exceeds a calibrated threshold.
abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) has made machine-generated text increasingly difficult to distinguish from human-written text. While recent studies explore leveraging internal representations of language models to uncover deeper detection signals, these raw features often exhibit substantial overlap between classes, limiting their discriminative power. To address this challenge, we propose Steer-to-Detect (\texttt{S2D}), a two-stage framework for detecting LLM-generated text. In the first stage, \texttt{S2D} learns a steering vector that is injected into the hidden states of a frozen observer LLM, producing representations with improved class separability. In the second stage, detection is performed via a hypothesis testing procedure based on the steered representations. We establish finite-sample, high-probability guarantees for Type I and Type II errors, providing a theoretical characterization of the procedure. Empirically, \texttt{S2D} achieves strong and consistent performance across a range of settings, including out-of-distribution scenarios and adversarial perturbations.
